subject: Week 23: book the 6-month well visit; window opens Oct 26
bodyText:
This week
Days 159-165 are the run-up to the half-year mark. Expect pushing up on straight arms in tummy time and sitting with support — independent sitting is emerging for some, but the CDC checkpoint for sitting without support is 9 months, so propped sitting is fully on-curve. Listen for turn-taking vocalization, squealing, and increasingly varied babble; he should be anticipating familiar routines and starting to look for partially hidden objects.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Mild constipation when solids begin — offer small sips of water from a cup and fiber-forward purees (pear, prune).
- [monitor] Persistent reflux with back-arching during feeds — document and raise at the 6-month visit; a GI consult is the escalation path.
- [call within 24h] First reaction to a new food: rash spreading beyond the mouth, hives, or vomiting within two hours of ingestion.
- [call now] Anaphylaxis after an allergen — facial swelling, breathing difficulty, hives plus vomiting, or sudden lethargy — call 911. Introduce allergens at home, in daytime, never solo.

Enrichment opportunities
- Register with Stanford SVNDL this weekend if you never did — the study's eligibility ceiling is 6 months, so the window closes around Nov 7; free structured 1:1 sessions, and the signup takes minutes. Stanford SVNDL participation: https://svndl.stanford.edu/participate/
- Set the solids plan if you are starting at 6 months: readiness signals are sitting with minimal support, a retired tongue-thrust reflex, and active interest in your food. Weight the first rotation toward iron — fortified oatmeal, pureed meats, lentils — because iron stores in breastfed infants deplete around 6 months. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Pull the high chair up to the table for one family meal a day from the first spoonful — the family-meal context builds long-run eating norms and adds live language exposure at zero cost.
- Keep reading at 30 min/day cumulative, split across bedtime, bath, and one daytime block — the dose is what compounds, not the book list. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26–Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit — book now. Vaccines: RV #3 (if RV5), DTaP #3, Hib #3 (if PRP-T), PCV #3, plus seasonal influenza #1; iron/hemoglobin screen and a solids-readiness check.
- Day 180 (Nov 7, 2026): the 6-month program windows open — paid swim conversion, ISR instructor contact, Suzuki instrument decision. Full brief lands that week.
- RSV season (Oct–Mar) is underway — refresh the daycare sick-policy and household visitor rules this month.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Supports whole weight on legs when held standing
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Builds leg strength for eventual pulling-to-stand. Does not need to bear weight independently.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/supports-weight-on-legs/complete

- Moves things from one hand to the other
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Bilateral coordination across the midline. Often accompanied by mouthing the transferred object.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/transfers-objects-hand-to-hand/complete

- Closes lips to show she doesn't want more food
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Pre-verbal refusal. Important to respect — supports developing satiety cues.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/closes-lips-not-more/complete

- Enjoys back-and-forth social play
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Active turn-taking in physical or vocal games. Distinct from earlier passive enjoyment of stimulation.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/enjoys-social-play/complete

- Sits without support
  AAP window: day 150-270
  What to look for: Hands free for play. WHO motor study cites 3.8-9.2 mo as the typical range.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-without-support/complete
